referenceSources.title: 1986 Volkswagen Scirocco 16V Tested: an Amazing Transformation
referenceSources.description:
A black second-generation Volkswagen Scirocco 16V is captured from behind, showcasing its sporty hatchback design. The body-colored rear bumper, flared fenders, and six-inch-wide alloy wheels with low-profile tires emphasize its performance upgrades. The manufacturer plate “24 M616” sits centrally on the tailgate, flanked by rectangular taillights and the Scirocco 16V badge.

This model was featured in a Car and Driver review highlighting its new twin-cam, sixteen-valve engine that delivers 123 horsepower and 120 lb-ft of torque. Performance figures include an eight-second sprint to 60 mph, a quarter-mile time of 15.9 seconds at 87 mph, and a top speed of 124 mph. Chassis enhancements such as vented front discs, rear disc brakes, and recalibrated suspension contribute to its handling prowess, making the Scirocco 16V a standout supercoupe of its era.
